(Retrieved via WebFetch, article text as returned; curl returned no paragraphs. The Times of Israel's own reporting)

With 89.8 percent of ballots counted as of Wednesday evening, the Central Elections Committee reported the following preliminary seat distribution in the 120-member Knesset:
Netanyahu's Bloc: 53 seats — Likud 26, Shas 7, United Torah Judaism 7, Otzma Yehudit 7, Religious Zionism 6.
Eisenkot's Bloc: 48 seats — Yashar 21, B'Yachad 12, The Democrats 8, Yisrael Beytenu 7.
Arab-led Parties: 19 seats — Joint List 12, Ra'am 7.
Netanyahu's coalition lost 15 seats compared to the current Knesset configuration. Arab parties nearly doubled their previous record of 10 seats, achieving an all-time high of 19 seats following record voter turnout in Arab communities.
Approximately 430,000 to 480,000 "double-envelope" ballots cast by soldiers, prisoners, diplomats, and others unable to vote at designated locations remained uncounted as of Wednesday evening. Counting of these ballots was scheduled to begin at 1 a.m. Thursday and conclude by Thursday evening, with final official results expected November 4.
Both blocs fell short of the 61-seat majority required to form a government independently.
